slot.brief: Compare radius or energy of the nth orbit of a hydrogen-like ion with that of hydrogen in the corresponding orbit, scaling with Z.

stem: Compare the radius of the third Bohr orbit of $\text{He}^+$ with that of hydrogen in the same orbit. What is the ratio $r_{\text{He}^+}/r_{\text{H}}$?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, the Bohr radius in orbit n is proportional to n²/Z. In the same orbit, helium has Z=2 and hydrogen has Z=1, so the ratio is 1/2.

working:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $r_n\propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.
At the same $n$, $\dfrac{r_{\text{He}^+}}{r_{\text{H}}}=\dfrac{Z_{\text{H}}}{Z_{\text{He}^+}}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, the Bohr radius in orbit n is proportional to n²/Z. In the same orbit, helium has Z=2 and hydrogen has Z=1, so the ratio is 1/2.
solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $r_n\propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$. At the same $n=3$, hydrogen has $Z=1$ and $\text{He}^+$ has $Z=2$:
$$\frac{r_{\text{He}^+}}{r_{\text{H}}}=\frac{1}{2}.$$
